name: fill_form
description: Fill multiple form fields in a single call on the active tab. Each entry in `fields` describes one field by its observation index and the action to take. Covers the four mechanics that handle ~95% of HTML forms: text input ('type'), dropdown selection ('select'), checkbox toggle ('check' / 'uncheck'), and radio click ('click'). Fields are applied in order. Optionally clicks a submit button at the end. The actor framework stops the batch at the first failing action; the result envelope's standard error string identifies which action failed and the post-batch observation shows the resulting page state — re-issue single-field tools (BrowserType / BrowserSelectOption / BrowserClick) for any field that didn't apply. All fields must be on the same tab. Cap: 50 fields per call.

inputs.name: fields
inputs.description: Ordered list of field operations. Each entry is an object with: `index` (integer, required) — element index from the latest observation; `action` (string, required) — one of 'type' | 'select' | 'check' | 'uncheck' | 'click'; `value` (string) — required for action='type' or 'select', ignored otherwise. For 'type', the existing field content is replaced. For 'select', value must match an <option>'s `value` attribute exactly. For 'check'/'uncheck', the action is a no-op if the checkbox is already in the desired state.

inputs.name: submit_index
inputs.description: Optional element index of a submit/continue button to click after all fields are filled. If omitted, leaves the form open. If any field failed and stop_on_error=false, the submit is skipped (safer default — partial submits are usually wrong).

inputs.name: stop_on_error
inputs.description: Reserved for forward compatibility. In v1 the actor framework always stops the batch at the first failing field — the flag is accepted but has no effect. Future versions may add a best-effort 'attempt every field, return per-field results' path.
